parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
Hello, and thanks to everyone for being on time. The meeting will be fairly short, and we will only be looking at fire procedures today. I had a similar meeting with the senior fire officers earlier, but you're all here because you've volunteered to act as fire wardens for your particular department. For some of you, this will be your first time in the role, although you’ve probably taken part in several fire drills since you’ve been here.

But now that the construction work is finished and we have a couple of new corridors and stairways, we need this meeting to update everyone.

Before I forget, you might have noticed some upgrades last week. The handheld fire extinguishers and the standard ones on the wall are all working well, as is the overhead sprinkler system. But the old alarm system has been replaced and should be a lot more reliable. Anyway, as fire wardens, you have a number of responsibilities.

Okay, those wardens responsible for the factory buildings, you’ll remember we had a minor fire back in January. Luckily, the fire doors around the room stopped most of the smoke from getting out, but the alarm should have been pressed much earlier. From what I understand, staff felt somewhat reluctant to activate it themselves and were looking for someone senior. So, please ensure that everyone knows it’s their responsibility to take action immediately. Can you also make sure that anyone who’s been hired since then has read the fire notices?

And wardens for office departments, you’ll also need to have a word with your staff. When the fire alarm went off in January, people got out of the office building pretty quickly — good! — but once they were out, they stood right in front of the doors. So, if the fire crews had needed to access the offices, they would have been blocked. It’s good to see that everyone had left their bags and stuff behind, though.

Okay, next on the agenda, there are a few aspects of fire safety that we need to go through with all of you wardens. Firstly, we want to make sure that when we have the next fire drill, there’s nothing blocking the escape routes. No obstacles, I mean. So, please check that as soon as possible. We want to be able to get outside very quickly.

One thing that should definitely be on your to-do list is making sure no one has locked the fire doors and that it’s easy to get through them.

Now, you might remember that last year we had a fire officer come and show us what to do if we see a colleague starting to suffer from the effects of smoke inhalation. Well, the same officer is coming back to lead another session.

Another issue is how to handle the fire extinguishers. Someone from the local fire department has booked in to teach people how to do that. I think it would be a good idea for fire wardens and department staff to attend those sessions.

Let’s see, what else is on the list? Oh yes, the evacuation points: the green area behind the main car park, the pavement on Hunter Street, and the unused area behind the factory car park. Fire wardens need to make sure all staff are familiar with these locations for evacuation, so please send out emails directly after the meeting.

And the last point is about flammable liquids. I believe there have been a few concerns about where they were being stored in the warehouse, but that’s been resolved now. However, if anyone has anything else to report, do let me know.

questions.question: ensuring there are no obstacles in fire escape routes

analyses.content: Firstly, we want to make sure that when we have the next fire drill, there’s nothing blocking the escape routes. No obstacles, I mean. So, please check that as soon as possible.
这里没有提到外人，全是针对 "you"（防火管理员）的要求。
发言人要求大家尽快（as soon as possible）检查逃生路线是否有障碍物，这意味着这是防火管理员需要优先处理的事。

questions.question: checking that fire doors are easily opened

analyses.content: 确保防火门容易打开且没被锁上，这绝对应该在你的任务清单（to-do list）上。
One thing that should definitely be on your to-do list is making sure no one has locked the fire doors and that it’s easy to get through them.
听到 "to-do list" 就要反应过来这是你需要做的工作，而不是不需要关注（C）或别人做（B）。

questions.question: showing staff how to look after each other

analyses.content: Now, you might remember that last year we had a fire officer come and show us what to do ... Well, the same officer is coming back to lead another session.
既然是 officer coming back，就不是防火管理员自己教，也不是不需要注意。
去年来过的那位消防官员（fire officer）会再次回来主持关于吸入烟雾处理的会议，属于外部专家负责。

questions.question: training staff to use fire extinguishers correctly

analyses.content: Another issue is how to handle the fire extinguishers. Someone from the local fire department has booked in to teach people how to do that.
虽然建议管理员去参加，但负责“教”（teach）这件事的是消防局的人。
关于灭火器的使用，已经预约了当地消防局（local fire department）的人来教大家，这也是外部专家。

questions.question: checking that staff are aware of evacuation points

analyses.content: Fire wardens need to make sure all staff are familiar with these locations for evacuation, so please send out emails directly after the meeting.
注意听 "Fire wardens need to make sure..." 以及 "send out emails directly"，强调了你们的直接责任。
发言人要求防火管理员在会后直接（directly）发邮件通知大家疏散点的位置，这是管理员的优先任务。

questions.question: checking that flammable liquids are properly stored

analyses.content: And the last point is about flammable liquids. I believe there have been a few concerns about where they were being stored in the warehouse, but that’s been resolved now.
听到 "concerns" 别急着选 A，重点是后面的转折 "but that's been resolved now"。
关于易燃液体的存储问题，发言人说这已经解决了（been resolved now），所以不需要再特别关注。
